title: Buried Saturday brunch scheduling
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by verifying that Anticipy can surface a buried scheduling intent from an uploaded audio file via ASR, rather than requiring a live microphone or text input.

v7_target.surface_rule: Must use user's real signed-in Anticipy surface on the same machine where the engine runs.
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must be captured from the public build's fresh surface render, including visible browser tabs and app windows, with timestamps matching the run.

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage is the primary proof path because it allows the engine to process a pre-recorded conversational snippet offline, testing the ASR pipeline without depending on real-time microphone permissions.

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Browser
real_user_surfaces.surface: macOS Desktop Chrome signed into user's Google account with HubSpot tab open or accessible
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: At least one visible tab showing HubSpot or a fresh screenshot of the Chrome window with the relevant record.

real_user_surfaces.name: Anticipy App
real_user_surfaces.surface: Public Anticipy app window after sign-in and onboarding
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Anticipy interface with user's dashboard and status indicators.

moments.description: Open the public Anticipy URL, complete sign-in and onboarding, and confirm the downloadable engine is available.
Verify that the user's real signed-in Chrome and Anticipy surfaces are visible and accessible. If not, record the missing surface and do not proceed.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Yeah, the kids were a handful this morning. Oh, before I forget, I really should set up Saturday brunch with Dana at the new place on Hawthorne, she wanted to catch up before her trip. Anyway, please add a follow-up note in HubSpot under the Brunch outreach record so I don't lose track. If you cannot prove the visible HubSpot surface, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: Generate a fresh audio file using the 'say' command on macOS, speaking the entire spoken_reference_text at normal pace. Save as an mp3 and upload via /api/listen/upload. Each run must produce a new file to avoid stale-artifact proofs.

moments.description: After ASR completes, the engine must check whether the transcribed text contains an actionable intent that matches a known surface (HubSpot). If no surface is provably visible, the engine should prepare a decline.

The engine must produce one of the three outcomes: act (by adding the note to HubSpot), ask (for clarification or permissions), or decline (if HubSpot surface is not provably visible). The output must include a proof artifact (screenshot or log) showing the decision and its reason.

After the run, the driver evaluates whether ASR-based audio upload uncovered any surface that would have been invisible to live-mic or paste-only modes. Note any gaps in the script's coverage of alternative input fidelities.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the uploaded audio and transcribes the spoken reference text with acceptable accuracy.
The engine identifies the buried scheduling intent and either acts on the HubSpot surface (if visible) or correctly declines with a clear reason.
The corresponding proof (screenshot, log, or API response) is from the real user's signed-in surfaces, not from a mocked or cloned environment.
The script completes all six moments in order, with no unhandled exceptions or skipped steps.
The final state confirms that audio upload as primary input fidelity works end-to-end for ambient intent extraction.
failure_triggers: The uploaded audio file fails to transcribe or returns garbage text.
The engine attempts to act on a surface that is not provably visible at the time of execution (e.g., stale screenshot or fake HubSpot tab).
The proof artifact is from a different build or run, violating freshness requirements.
The real user's Anticipy surface is not available (e.g., no signed-in browser profile), causing the script to abort early.
The engine chooses 'ask' or 'decline' without providing a human-readable justification tied to the surface state.
